items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWEE] I'm trying to think of the young lady's name who sang on some of those -- but I can't think of it right now. >> [INTERVIEWER] It wasn't Helen ... [INTERVIEWEE] No.

ctx.x: We had a lot of Ellington's men on them.
Yep. I got some with Helen Humes; I got some with Charlie Christian; whoever was in town, you used them on bass, and was gracious that remembered me from Chicago and used me.

But when you started that big band, you called me and offered me a job, and I don't know if you remember that, Teddy, but you're such a beautiful human being, and I got to tell you this, man, and it's got to go down as a matter of record and when you called and said, 'Milt, I'd like to have you join us, because I'd been making records with you and like you so much,' and the salary wasn't going to be the same salary that I was making with Cab -- but of course, I couldn't take a cut, and I said thank you -- and you…

items.title: 67255_Helen Humes oral history interview
items.q: They had Benny Goodman, Teddy Wilson, and Milt Harry Hinton, Shelly Mann, / Edison. Lockjaw was there.

ctx.x: All three there. And then later on we had Art Tatum. And then I had Teddy Wilson, and . . .
